body.statement: Whenever \(\mathcal M_{T_0,T_1}(0)\ne\varnothing\), there are constants \(0<c<C<\infty\), depending only on the fixed dimensions, \(\alpha\), and the stated bounded class constants, such that for every \(T_0,T_1\) and every nonempty margin stratum, \(c\rho_{\mathrm{ad}}(\gamma)\le R_{\mathrm{ad}}(\gamma)\le\sup_{\vartheta\in\mathcal M_{T_0,T_1}(\gamma)}\mathbb E_\vartheta[\operatorname{diam}_2\{\widehat{\mathcal C}_{\mathrm{ad}}\}]\le C\rho_{\mathrm{ad}}(\gamma)\). The lower bound is obtained from legal pairs in the original full-panel Gaussian experiment, including constant-post-factor compensated loading rotations, direct post-noise pairs, and bounded-signal saturation pairs.
body.justification: This is the first sharp expected-diameter frontier for a full sparse causal-effect vector when the decoding operator is learned from the same panel.
body.gap: NicklVanDeGeer2013 characterizes sparse-vector honesty with an observed regression design; it does not contain the pre-panel loading-rotation channel or the \(\kappa_s(L)\)-indexed bounded-signal frontier.
body.consumer: It quantifies the shortest globally valid full-vector uncertainty achievable in the fixed-factor analyses of HeLiShiMiao2026.
body.proof_tex:
Write \(a_0=T_0^{-1/2}\), \(a_1=T_1^{-1/2}\), and \(e=\lVert\widehat P-P\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\).  We first prove the upper bound on every sample, including samples on which the true parameter is not accepted.  Take two elements \(b,b'\in\widehat{\mathcal C}_{\mathrm{ad}}\), with witnesses \((P',m',r')\) and \((P'',m'',r'')\), where
\[
z=m'+b+r'=m''+b'+r'',\;
\lVert r'\rVert_2,\lVert r''\rVert_2\le\varepsilon_1.
\]
Set \(h=b-b'\).  It is supported on at most \(2s\) coordinates.  Since \(P'm'=m'\), \(P''m''=m''\), and both accepted projectors are within \(\delta_0\) of \(\widehat P\),
\[
\lVert(I_N-P)m'\rVert_2
\le\lVert P'-P\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\lVert m'\rVert_2
\le A(\delta_0+e),
\]
and the same bound holds for \(m''\).  Projecting
\(h=m''-m'+r''-r'\) onto \(L^\perp\), and using the margin condition, gives, for \(\gamma>0\),
\[
\gamma\lVert h\rVert_2
\le\lVert(I_N-P)h\rVert_2
\le2A(\delta_0+e)+2\varepsilon_1.
\]
Independently, the cube and triangle inequalities give
\[
\lVert h\rVert_2\le2B\sqrt{s},
\;
\lVert h\rVert_2\le\lVert m'-m''\rVert_2+\lVert r'-r''\rVert_2
\le2A+2\varepsilon_1.
\]
Therefore
\[
\operatorname{diam}_2(\widehat{\mathcal C}_{\mathrm{ad}})
\le\min\left\{2B\sqrt{s},\,2A+2\varepsilon_1,
{2\varepsilon_1+2A(\delta_0+e)\over\gamma}\right\},
\]
with the quotient omitted at \(\gamma=0\).  The pre-panel lemma and the definitions imply, for a fixed-class constant \(C_0\),
\[
\varepsilon_1\le C_0a_1,\;
\delta_0+\mathbb Ee\le C_0a_0.
\]
Taking expectations in the pathwise display and using
\[
\min\{A+a_1,x\}\le a_1+\min\{A,x\}
\]
shows
\[
\sup_{\vartheta\in\mathcal M_{T_0,T_1}(\gamma)}
\mathbb E_\vartheta\operatorname{diam}_2(\widehat{\mathcal C}_{\mathrm{ad}})
\le C\min\left\{B\sqrt{s},a_1+\min\left[A,{a_1+Aa_0\over\gamma}\right]\right\}
=C\rho_{\mathrm{ad}}(\gamma).
\]
At \(\gamma=0\), the same conclusion follows from the \(2A+2\varepsilon_1\) bound and the prescribed infinite-quotient convention.  Global honesty was proved above, so the definition of \(R_{\mathrm{ad}}\) gives the first upper inequality.

We next prove a full-observation lower bound.  We use the following elementary two-point fact.  If a confidence set has coverage at least \(1-\alpha\) at laws \(Q_0,Q_1\), with corresponding targets \(b_0,b_1\), then
\[
\mathbb E_{Q_0}\operatorname{diam}_2(\mathcal C)
\ge\lVert b_1-b_0\rVert_2\{1-2\alpha-\operatorname{TV}(Q_0,Q_1)\}.
\]
Indeed, under \(Q_0\), the event \(b_0\in\mathcal C\) has probability at least \(1-\alpha\), and the event \(b_1\in\mathcal C\) has probability at least \(1-\alpha-\operatorname{TV}(Q_0,Q_1)\); intersect them.  For equal-covariance Gaussian vectors with mean difference \(v\) and covariance \(\sigma^2I\), completing the square gives Hellinger affinity \(\exp\{-\lVert v\rVert_2^2/(8\sigma^2)\}\).  Cauchy--Schwarz applied to the two square-root densities gives
\[
\operatorname{TV}(Q_0,Q_1)
\le\sqrt{1-\exp\{-\lVert v\rVert_2^2/(4\sigma^2)\}}.
\]
Thus a sufficiently small fixed upper bound on the full Gaussian squared mean distance divided by \(\sigma^2\) makes the brace a positive fixed constant.

We construct three legal pairs.  Nonemptiness of \(\mathcal M_{T_0,T_1}(0)\) supplies one admissible \(D,F,\sigma\); these constraints are independent of the chosen loading frame, and all post factors below are constant.  First keep \(U,D,F,m=0,\sigma\) fixed, take \(\beta_0=0\), and take \(\beta_1=te_j\).  The pre means agree and the squared full post-mean distance is \(T_1t^2\).  With a sufficiently small fixed constant \(c_1>0\),
\[
t=c_1\min\{B,\sigma T_1^{-1/2}\}
\]
gives the lower term \(\min\{B,a_1\}\); both points lie in the same margin stratum.

Second, compactness in the finite support minimum gives, for a loading space with \(\kappa_s(L)=\gamma\), a unit vector \(h\) supported on at most \(2s\) such that
\[
\lVert(I_N-P)h\rVert_2=\gamma,\;
\lVert Ph\rVert_2=\sqrt{1-\gamma^2}.
\]
Such a loading space exists for every \(\gamma\in[0,\kappa_\star]\): the real Grassmannian is connected, \(L\mapsto\kappa_s(L)\) is continuous, a space containing a coordinate vector has margin zero, and a Vandermonde frame has strictly positive margin; compactness then makes its image the full interval from zero to its maximum.  Split the support of \(h\) into two parts of size at most \(s\), so that \(th=\beta_1-\beta_0\) with both effects bounded whenever \(t\le B\).  Put
\[
m_0={t\over2}Ph,\; m_1=-{t\over2}Ph.
\]
The pre laws coincide, while the difference between every post mean column is
\[
(m_1+\beta_1)-(m_0+\beta_0)=t(I_N-P)h
\]
exactly.  Hence the full squared mean distance is \(T_1t^2\gamma^2\).  Taking
\[
t=c_2\min\{B,A,\sigma/(\gamma\sqrt{T_1})\}
\]
for a sufficiently small fixed \(c_2\), with the quotient infinite at zero, gives the lower term
\[
\min\{B,A,a_1/\gamma\}.
\]

Third suppose \(\gamma>0\), use the same minimizing \(h\), and write
\[
h=\rho v+\gamma w,\;
\rho=\sqrt{1-\gamma^2},\quad v\in L,\quad w\in L^\perp,\quad
\lVert v\rVert_2=\lVert w\rVert_2=1.
\]
The dimension condition implies \(\kappa_\star^2\le(N-2s)/N<1\): averaging \(\operatorname{tr}(U_C^{\top}U_C)/r\) over all \((N-2s)\)-subsets \(C\) gives \((N-2s)/N\), and \(\lambda_{\min}\le\operatorname{tr}/r\).  Thus \(\rho>0\).  Let \(M=A/2\), set
\[
m_0=Mv,\; m_1=m_0-th,
\]
and choose \(t\le\min\{B,A/8\}\).  Then \(3A/8\le\lVert m_1\rVert_2\le5A/8\).  Let \(R\) be the rotation in \(\operatorname{span}(v,w)\) that maps \(v\) to \(m_1/\lVert m_1\rVert_2\) and is the identity on the orthogonal complement, and put \(U_1=RU_0\), retaining \(D,F,\sigma\).  Then \(m_1\in\operatorname{col}(U_1)\), and the angle \(\theta\) of this rotation satisfies
\[
\sin\theta={t\gamma\over\lVert m_1\rVert_2}
\le {8t\gamma\over3A}.
\]
Split \(th=\beta_1-\beta_0\) as above.  Since \(m_1=m_0-th\), all post mean columns are exactly equal under the two points.  The pre contribution to the full Gaussian squared mean distance is
\[
\lVert(U_1-U_0)DF\rVert_F^2
=T_0\lVert(U_1-U_0)D\rVert_F^2
\le2T_0d_{\mathrm{hi}}^2\sin^2\theta
\le {128T_0d_{\mathrm{hi}}^2t^2\gamma^2\over9A^2}.
\]
The first point belongs to the \(\gamma\)-stratum; the second is in the global class, which is exactly what global honesty requires.  Taking
\[
t=c_3\min\{B,A,A\sigma/(d_{\mathrm{hi}}\gamma\sqrt{T_0})\}
\]
with a sufficiently small fixed \(c_3\) gives the lower term
\[
\min\{B,A,Aa_0/\gamma\}.
\]
At \(\gamma=0\), the null vector supplied by the sparse-uniqueness proof gives identical full laws and the term \(\min\{B,A\}\).

All these are pairs in the original \((Y_0,Y_1)\) experiment; no noiseless label or oracle loading space has been supplied.  Finally, for nonnegative \(x,y\),
\[
\min\{A,x+y\}\asymp
\max\{\min(A,x),\min(A,y)\},
\]
and \(a_1+q\asymp\max(a_1,q)\), with absolute comparison factors at most two.  Applying these identities with \(x=a_1/\gamma\), \(y=Aa_0/\gamma\), and observing that fixed \(s\) makes \(B\sqrt{s}\asymp B\), the maximum of the three lower terms is comparable to \(\rho_{\mathrm{ad}}(\gamma)\).  The two-point inequality therefore gives \(R_{\mathrm{ad}}(\gamma)\ge c\rho_{\mathrm{ad}}(\gamma)\), uniformly in \(T_0,T_1,\gamma\).  Together with the upper construction, this proves the theorem, including post-noise, compensated-rotation, and bounded-signal saturation channels.
